survivingClaim: Precise obstruction (equivalence with no unconditional hypothesis; Landau target in twisted form). For fixed s = sigma+it, 1/2 < sigma < 1, t != 0: the Laplace transform in log P of G(P;s) is (1/w)[log((s+w-1)zeta(s+w)) - log(s-1) - H(s+w)] with singular points w = 0 and w = rho - s for every zero at every height. An upper bound Re G <= C P^alpha for all large P at that one point gives beta <= max(sigma+alpha, beta_t) for every zero; a lower bound Re G >= -C P^alpha gives Theta <= sigma+alpha (the referee's argument shows no exceptional ordinate for this sign); conversely Theta <= sigma+alpha gives the two-sided bound O(P^(alpha+eps)). G_lambda = -G_zeta identically, which rules out one-sided derivations that use only complete multiplicativity, real unimodular local parameters and meromorphy, but not derivations using the functional equation. The claim that no unconditional input gives a one-sided bound without the two-sided one is a survey (ARGUED), not a theorem. Measured (float64, P <= 1e7, plus referee rerun to 4e6 at other points): the zero term has size P^(beta-sigma)/(|s-rho| log P), seen on U, RZ_b and DH near their zeros, with monotone descent at t = gamma; controls with the zero at distance >= 500 are not separated from zeta; the zeta table restates verified height. No statement about zeros of zeta is established.
obstruction: The Laplace transform in log P of G(P;s) has singular points w = 0 and w = rho - s for every zero at every height, so a one-sided bound Re G <= C P^alpha or >= -C P^alpha at one fixed point is equivalent (up to eps, with the exceptional ordinate t = gamma for the upper sign) to Theta <= sigma + alpha: the Landau target of rows T2/P10 in twisted form. No unconditional input is known to give the one-sided bound without the two-sided one (survey, argued). The step from fixed P to all P is the statement to be proved.
